source: User-uploaded TDN research audit, Pasted text.txt, file_00000000008c81f8844baf3fa3e94e95
scope: Every named stage, four architecture mechanisms, six literature experimental questions, and the deployment-policy extension
interpretation: Requirements are declared before new full-cohort measurement. A completed computation is not a scientific success. Each question must expose independently resolved errors, uncertainty, controls, and limitations.

system.host_cpu: AMD Ryzen 7800X3D, 8 physical cores, 16 scheduled threads
system.account: profile-defined optional local account; no CARC account inheritance
system.path_policy: All project outputs, caches, temporary files, and reports stay inside the checkout. No /tmp or /scratch1.
system.allocation_policy: Per-stage allocations must fit 110000 MiB scheduler memory. Short stages, no pending-job cap, no automatic budget expansion, no 20-hour neural allocation. Preserve an 18 GiB and 75% initially-free/total VRAM soft limit. Host/shared memory is not extra VRAM.

questions.literature_direction: Non-asymptotic splitting, large gradients, stiff order reduction
questions.literal_question: When does cubic defect scaling stop being an adequate finite-step model?
required_measurements: Independent FP64 coupled defect at multiple step sizes
Symmetric positive/negative perturbations and background subtraction
Uncertainty propagated after division by amplitude squared
Gate-only and gate-plus-constant least-squares residuals
Actual bounded-map temporal fit and nonlinear-time control
Crossed reaction, diffusion, amplitude, step size, mean and spectra
questions.interpretation: Separate small-step local order, finite-step representability, and stiff accuracy; a cubic prefactor does not establish stiff order.

questions.literature_direction: Exponential integrators and stiff order conditions
questions.literal_question: Which input/output diffusion scales must the learned kernel retain?
required_measurements: Actual discrete diffusion eigenvalues for both input modes and output mode
Mode pairs with the same output frequency and different input damping
Ablated input-only, output-only and full input/output-conditioned responses
Both Strang orientations against independently resolved strong-diffusion endpoints
Maximum-eigenvalue stiffness and spectral-gap homogenization separately
questions.interpretation: Diffusion-first strong-diffusion behavior is an established classical control; the learned eigenvalue-conditioned response is a hypothesis.

questions.literature_direction: Bilinear/Volterra operators, separable interaction kernels, learned exponential integrators
questions.literal_question: Can the pair kernel be compressed without losing phase-dependent response?
required_measurements: Offline rank 2, 4 and 8 response study before a trained-kernel interpretation
Mixed mode pairs with varied phases
Pair symmetry, Hermitian reality and translation-equivariance checks
Signed source dictionary and zero-preserving nonlocal transport
Count actual FFTs, local operator applications and complete-rollout cost
No multiplication of an already-quadratic pair branch by the existing quadratic gate
questions.interpretation: State nominal rank and expanded separable terms separately; neither low rank nor physical limits alone demonstrate accuracy or efficiency.

questions.literal_question: Which rough-field failures arise from representation mismatch rather than temporal error?
required_measurements: The same continuous initial field sampled onto paired grids
Separate same-grid discrete-accuracy and continuum-refinement tracks
Native circular-grid product and a declared dealiased product diagnostic
Actual Fourier-support masks, not only identical mode integers
Near-Nyquist, rough, mixed/high-input-to-low-output pairs
Document information bypasses, including a full-state physical source into a precompressed encoder
questions.interpretation: A changed product or dealiased solver is a changed target; do not pool its errors with the original finite-difference discrete target.

questions.literal_question: Can a validated estimator eventually replace reference-informed step selection?
required_measurements: Estimator and thresholds fitted on development/calibration parents only
Independent endpoint accuracy of accepted predictions
Reference uncertainty and both RMS and maximum norms
Composition agreement compared against an independent teacher
Accept/reject decisions, false-acceptance denominator and rates
Frozen thresholds and no fresh-reference-informed acceptance decisions
questions.interpretation: Report an empirical audited policy, not a certified error estimator. Agreement of two wrong predictions is insufficient.

questions.literal_question: Can unequal unseen steps remain accurate, rather than merely self-consistent?
required_measurements: Equal and unequal step compositions at the same final time
Genuinely unseen step sizes not used for training or validation selection
Independent resolved endpoints and composition-consistency error separately
Multiple step orderings with crossed stiffness
Complete-rollout accuracy and timed work including all substeps
questions.interpretation: Self-consistency is an auxiliary diagnostic, not an endpoint accuracy target.

questions.literature_direction: Deployment acceptance, rejected work and classical fallback
questions.literal_question: Does an independently audited acceptance policy improve actual complete-solver accuracy and cost after rejected work and classical fallback?
required_measurements: Fresh held-out accept/reject outcomes with independent teacher errors
False acceptances at each declared RMS and maximum target
Rejected neural and estimator work
Classical fallback calls and measured cost
Total accepted-plus-rejected-plus-fallback work
Comparison against directly running ETDRK4 and fused GL3
If estimator work is shared, distinguish actual benchmark work from selected-component policy cost estimates; do not label an attributed sum as independently timed standalone policy wall-clock work.
questions.interpretation: Post-hoc reference frontiers and deployable policy frontiers are distinct outputs. No claimed benefit may omit rejected work or fallback cost.

mechanisms.name: Source before spatial transport
requirements: Zero-preserving transport of physically vanishing commutator-derived sources
Compare local gate, gate plus constant, filtered source, and signed-source dictionary
Use uniform backgrounds, single modes, phase-varied mixed modes and remote bumps
Arbitrary finite-weight zero limits for homogeneous fields, zero reaction, zero diffusion and zero time
Report quadratic spatial-shape residual and flat-receiver response

mechanisms.name: Phase-aware stiffness-conditioned pair interaction
requirements: Condition on h times the actual discrete input and output diffusion eigenvalues, reaction and mean
Rank 2, 4 and 8 offline study and learned controls
Preserve input phases, pair symmetry, real output and declared product convention
Do not raise quadratic response to fourth order with an additional quadratic gate
Report every transform and effective expanded factor count

mechanisms.name: Base solver strong-diffusion orientation
requirements: Reaction-first R(h/2)D(h)R(h/2) and diffusion-first D(h/2)R(h)D(h/2)
Independent cross of diffusion, reaction, h, mean and amplitude
Strong-diffusion limit R(h, mean(u0)) on connected periodic grids
Separate global homogenization from high-frequency stiffness
Full-rollout timing with actual feasible half-step fusion recorded

mechanisms.name: Dynamical mean-variance closure
requirements: Exact instantaneous mean derivative r*(c-c*c-V)
Exact instantaneous variance derivative 2*mean(v*L(v))+2*r*(1-2*c)*V-2*r*mean(v*v*v)
Bounded moment representation and explicit approximate evolution/integration
Compare existing arbitrary mean head and existing spectral-mean classical correction
Fields with equal means and variances but different spectra and phases
Keep phase-dependent spatial kernel separate from moment energy summaries

stages.name: structure
must_expose: Gate-span representational obstruction above reference uncertainty
Temporal representability through actual bounded map
Strong-diffusion orientations
Offline pair rank
Exact mean/variance law and phase/spectrum diagnostics

stages.name: prepare
must_expose: Accepted independent FP64 teachers
Parent-disjoint training/validation/calibration/confirmation manifests
Training-only normalization
Continuous field/grid provenance
Frozen pre-confirmation success criteria

stages.name: controls
must_expose: Gate-placement and nonlinear-time changes separately and together
Both orientations
Current gate and arbitrary mean-head anchors
Closure versus spectral-mean and classical controls

stages.name: optimize
must_expose: Bounded learning-rate and batch alternatives
Gradient norms, correction magnitudes and losses by regime
Physical defect scales
Validation-only checkpoint selection including initialization
No longer training as an assumed fix

stages.name: compression
must_expose: Trained source-constrained premix versus precompression
Physical treatment, data, initialization and selection paired
Matched actual spectral support
Parameter-matched FNO and measured-cost comparison separately
Information bypass inventory
Initialization-selected pairs inconclusive

stages.name: kernel
must_expose: Offline rank evidence retained even if negative
Rank 2, 4 and 8 independently selected trained arms
Economical representation versus fused GL3 rollout cost
Mixed-phase and stiff-response accuracy

stages.name: confirm
must_expose: Fresh continuous parents sampled on paired grids
Genuinely unseen equal and unequal steps
Crossed amplitude, variance, spectrum, diffusion and reaction
Rough/Nyquist RMS and maximum coverage
Independent mean/spatial errors and base regressions
Complete-solver ETDRK4 and fused GL3 frontiers

stages.name: policy
must_expose: Frozen calibration-only estimator and thresholds
False-acceptance counts/rates and denominators
Rejected neural/estimator work and measured fallback
Independent accepted endpoint RMS/maximum accuracy
Total policy work and direct classical controls

common_requirements.requirement: All named scientific questions must have actual executable records, including null/negative/inconclusive findings; a documentation-only mapping does not implement a question.
Freeze protocol, sources, software, profiles, prerequisite seals, splits and success criteria before fresh confirmation; development/full runs remain distinct.
Separate computational completion, numerical correctness, and scientific conclusions. Do not treat training or test success as a solver advantage.
Keep reference uncertainty, failed/infeasible cases, initialization selections and per-regime regressions visible. Repeated parent/seed/norm/schedule rows are paired descriptive evidence.
Use RMS and maximum norms separately; retain mean and spatial error components and compare matched uncertainty-aware tolerances.
Retain Strang, ETDRK4 and fused GL3 complete-solver controls; retain analytic spectral-mean correction for mean-closure comparison.
Keep training/inference FP32 and TF32 off, independent teachers FP64. Actual CUDA tests need a real allocated desktop GPU; cloud CPU evidence is not GPU validation.
Project reporting adapts to Tower; do not change Tower. Stage-specific JUnit files and declared science outputs must be published with exact provenance.

Established splitting, exponential/Volterra mechanisms and classical moment identities are not novel by relabeling. Local implementation deductions and new architecture hypotheses must be distinguished from measured results.

predeclared_success_criteria.interpretation: Operational preregistered criteria; no statistical significance or uniform superiority assertion.

full_confirmation_design.interpretation: Paired physical-factor cases and reused phase/seed clusters; not 32 independent random fields.
